finding.title: New task gives the reviewer an outcome that needs a file it may not write, with no note
finding.what_the_person_sees: No note at New task. The run ends with 'I am not allowed to write review.md' and the review grade is 10.
finding.expected: A note at New task, or a specialist that can write the file.
finding.suspected_cause: The who-note does not check the outcome's files against what the specialist may write.

verdict.root_cause: ADR 0109 says a reviewer writes no file and its findings are its report. That rule exists only as prompt text: the reviewer's registry entry and the planner's delegation rule in project-manager.md. Nothing in code applies it when the person makes the task. (1) New task's who-note (NewTaskDialog.tsx:369-378) shows only two things: `runsOn` (where it runs on which credential) and `limitation`. The daemon (model-settings-view.ts:189-193) sets `limitation` only to NO_WEB_LIMITATION for specialists that need the web. So picking `reviewer` with the outcome 'review.md lists the gaps and risks found in notes/plan.md' shows nothing. The dialog already sends the typed words to the daemon (TR-11), but nothing compares them with the reviewer's write rule. (2) The app also builds a criterion the reviewer cannot meet. A task with no criteria gets outcomeCriterion() (verification.ts:65-70): 'The work itself shows this outcome (a file, a page or an output, not only the report): …'. The brief (executor.ts:1126-1128) and the critic (critic.ts:482-484) both use it, for every specialist, the reviewer included. The bench log shows the reviewer got exactly that criterion, while its own prompt says 'You write no file, not even a review file a brief names'. The reviewer did what it was told, and the critic graded against the app's criterion. So this is not the model's choice. One caveat on the evidence: in this run the 'could not do' and the grade of 10 come mostly from notes/plan.md being missing, which the check's repro set up on purpose. The missing write right is the second reason. Even with the plan present, this task could not pass its criterion.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/pages/project/NewTaskDialog.tsx:369-378; packages/runtime/src/daemon/model-settings-view.ts:189-193; packages/runtime/src/loop/verification.ts:65-70 (used at packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1126-1128 and packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts:482-484); evals/registry/specialists/reviewer/specialist.md (the 'You write no file' paragraph)
verdict.fix_sketch: Daemon side, on the TR-11 words path of GET /settings/models: when a specialist's registry tools include no write tool (no cc:Write or cc:Edit; today that means the reviewer) and the typed outcome or criteria ask for a file (a path with an extension, or 'write/create … file'), return a note in the daemon's words. For example: 'The reviewer writes no file: its findings are its report, in the task's drawer. To have review.md written, choose the writer or Let the agent choose.' New task and Edit show it as task-who-note, the way the limitation note is shown today, and creating the task is not refused. Brief and critic side (ADR 0109 decision 1): for a specialist whose output is its report, outcomeCriterion should read 'The report shows this outcome: …' instead of '… not only the report'. That way a reviewer task the person makes with no criteria can pass on its findings. Update ADR 0109 (or add a note) and the maintainer docs for New task and verification.
verdict.failing_test_idea: apps/ui/test/tasks.test.tsx (the person's boundary): open New task, choose 'reviewer', type the outcome 'review.md lists the gaps and risks found in notes/plan.md'. Expect task-who-note to say the reviewer writes no file and its findings are its report. With the outcome 'lists the gaps and risks found in notes/plan.md', expect no note. Today the first case fails: task-who-note is null. Add a real-daemon case: GET /settings/models?project=…&outcome=review.md… returns the reviewer's note. Add a runtime executor-brief case: a reviewer task with no criteria gets no 'not only the report' criterion, and the critic's evidence carries the same criterion.
verdict.area_hint: No run C area covers this. It needs a small fix area for ADR 0109 on tasks the person makes (New task and Edit who-note, plus outcomeCriterion). The nearest existing area is l3-small, which owned L3-research-3.
verdict.notes: Evidence checked: lr-run.json and lr-look.json. In the bench database the task's specialist is 'reviewer', its outcome is 'review.md lists the gaps and risks found in notes/plan.md', and it has no criteria. In model-calls.jsonl the reviewer's brief has criterion 1 'The work itself shows this outcome (a file, a page or an output, not only the report): review.md …'. The reviewer's report says 'A review task that must produce review.md should go to a specialist allowed to write files.' The task check flagged the same thing but changed nothing. That is by design: the task was waiting for the person, and the task check's flagged lines are never shown to the person. The design doc §3.5 does not promise a who-note about write rights; ADR 0109 covered only the planner. So this is a gap in what the design covers, not a regression. I did not run the stand-in bench: the null note follows directly from the code, which has only the two note sources. Severity minor: it is cheap (CHF 0.04 here), the reviewer's report is honest about it, and the person was asked. The same thing would happen with a chat-made task or an Edit to reviewer.

Send answers -> Done line 'Done: Answers sent: "Add the club's phone number to contact.html" goes on with them; it joins the session that is running.', and the task re-ran in that session (C3-left-3 pass).
